source_quality.notes: text layer covers all 23 pages; figures read from the text around them

task_reconstruction: Build a total scarcity metric that splits physical from economic scarcity, check it on 83 countries, forecast Pakistan to 2030, and test an intervention plan.

section_map.summary: summary of the metric, the forecast and the plan
the bleak scene, the blame and the aim
seven assumptions and the variable table
the review of the existing indicators
the physical metric from the adjusted criticality ratio
the economic metric from five weighted factors
the mix of the two metrics and the check on 83 countries
the case of Pakistan and its drivers
the intervention plan and its test
the conclusions, the strengths and the weaknesses

contributions.summary: the criticality ratio adjusted by a climate factor and by desalinated water
economic scarcity as one minus a grey-relational weighted sum of five factors
one parameter mixing the two scarcities, suggested at 1.1
a plan that lowers both scores for Pakistan while the class stays at 4

dependency_graph.relation: the adjusted ratio or the four-level index is the physical input
the flipped weighted sum is the economic input
the forecast withdrawals change the numerator in 2030

assumptions.summary: the published data are accurate, reliable and mutually consistent
the countries left out barely move the weights
environmental withdrawal is small and its data are missing
climate, renewable resources and irrigation efficiency stay fixed to 2030
industrial and municipal withdrawal per person depend only on income

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 83 countries taken at each one's latest available year
five factor weights computed by grey relational analysis
two log-log fits estimated on 169 countries
eleven yearly observations, 2004 to 2014, fed to the grey forecast

models.summary: criticality ratio adjusted by a climate factor
a one-parameter mix of the two metrics
two log-log fits of withdrawal per person on income

verification.summary: 83 countries compared by eye with the published scarcity map
the grey forecast reports a small error on each factor
the mixing parameter swept from 0.5 to 1.5 on eight countries

results_trace.summary: by 2030 the economic score falls from 0.5071 to 0.3395 and the adjusted ratio rises from 2.19 to 2.52
the plan lowers the economic score to 0.3179 and the adjusted ratio to 2.26
Sudan, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia rank worst

writing_logic.summary: the aim arrives only after the blame is laid
three indicators are reviewed and two are kept
the forecast is reported as one scarcity eased and one deepened
the close names the question left open

language_observations.summary: opens on a planet getting thirstier and thirstier
rejects a framework as too intricate to be understood and implemented
knocks down a false comfort with however, the truth is
ends on questions it admits it failed to chase

visualization_observations.summary: Table 4 reads the four-level index off the adjusted ratio and water per person
Figure 2 plots the two metrics and Figure 3 is the published map
Figure 5 plots the forecast metric against the mixing parameter
Figure 6 plots the metric with and without the plan

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: reviewing the standard indicators and saying why two were dropped reads as a real modelling choice
owning the dilemma between the two physical measures reads as honest rather than weak

weaknesses.summary: either physical measure loses something: ranking, or population
the forecast rests on many premises that may not hold
the verification sample may be too small
both withdrawal fits explain little of the variation

independent_extensions.summary: multiply a use-to-resource ratio by a weighted climate factor before classifying it
turn a higher-is-better weighted sum into a scarcity score by subtracting it from one

unresolved_questions: the grey forecasting recurrence is described but never written as a formula
the table boundaries are shifted from the source table with no stated rule
the suggested mixing value of 1.1 is read off the verification and not derived
no rule is given for how a country should choose its mixing parameter
both withdrawal fits are used despite low coefficients of determination
